title: Care for handtools, utensils and protective equipment

lessons.title: Using and checking hand tools and utensils
lessons.html:
Using and checking hand tools and utensils

At a silo or depot you use many hand tools and utensils every day: brooms, shovels, scoops, spanners, hammers, screwdrivers, knives, bag needles, sample buckets, sieves and grain probes. Good tools make the work easier and safer. Broken or dirty tools cause injuries and can make grain dirty.

Use the right tool for the job

  • Use a spanner of the right size, not pliers, for nuts.
  • Use a screwdriver to turn screws, not to open tins or as a chisel.
  • Use a grain scoop for grain, not a shovel that was used for mud or waste.
  • Use a sharp knife for cutting. A blunt knife needs more force and slips.

Check before use

  • Handles: not cracked, loose or splintered.
  • Heads: tight on the handle. A loose hammer head can fly off.
  • Blades: sharp and not chipped.
  • Sieves and probes: no holes, dents or blockages.
  • Clean: no old grain, chemicals or rust.

If a tool is damaged, do not use it. Put a tag on it and give it to your supervisor for repair or replacement.

Tool care after use

  1. Clean off dust, grain and dirt.
  2. Dry the tool to stop rust.
  3. Put a little oil on metal parts where needed.
  4. Cover blades.
  5. Return the tool to its place in the store or on the tool board.
  6. Sign it in if your site keeps a tool register.

Example

Zanele finds the head of the store's hammer is loose. She tags it, hands it in and uses another hammer. The next week the store has a new handle fitted. Nobody was hurt.

Tools are company property. Losing tools costs money. Look after them as if they were your own.

lessons.title: Caring for your protective equipment
lessons.html:
Caring for your protective equipment

Personal protective equipment (PPE) protects your body from hazards at work. Your employer must give you the PPE you need. You must wear it, keep it clean and report damage. This is part of your duty under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993.

Common PPE and how to care for it

PPECare
Safety bootsClean off mud and grain. Check soles and steel caps. Dry them away from direct heat.
Dust maskThrow away disposable masks when dirty, wet or hard to breathe through. Replace filters on re-usable masks as the instructions say.
Ear plugs and muffsKeep plugs clean. Wipe muff cushions. Replace cracked cushions.
Safety glassesClean with water and a soft cloth. Replace if scratched or cracked.
GlovesReplace when torn. Wash chemical gloves before taking them off.
OverallsWash regularly. Replace when torn.
HarnessCheck straps and buckles before every use. Hand in a harness that has stopped a fall.
Reflective vestKeep clean so it can be seen.

Storing PPE

  • Keep it in your locker or the PPE store, clean and dry.
  • Keep it out of the sun, which weakens plastic and rubber.
  • Keep masks in a clean bag so dust does not get inside.

Never

  • Never use damaged PPE.
  • Never change or cut your PPE.
  • Never share ear plugs or masks.
  • Never take chemical-dirty PPE home to wash with family clothes.

Key points

  • Use the right tool for each job.
  • Check tools before use and tag damaged ones.
  • Clean, dry and return tools after use.
  • Wear your PPE, keep it clean and store it dry.
  • Report and replace damaged PPE.
